caption: The drawing depicts a wooden window set into a wall. The window features two shutters: the left shutter is open, showing five vertical, brown, turned wooden bars spaced evenly apart and supported by three horizontal blueish wooden rails, while the right shutter is closed and consists of flat wooden panels painted in a faded blue-green color. Both shutters are framed with the same blue-green painted wood, and the right shutter is fitted with three metallic hinges and a latch, all depicted in a muted brown color. Additional metal fastenings appear on the middle and bottom of the shutters. The surrounding wall is off-white with subtle brown shading to suggest texture. The opened left shutter extends outward from the window plane, and the entire window is set against a plain, light background.
title: Window Shutters and Details
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
